title: Yaroslavl/Vologda P104
description:
C type short antenna summer coverage
Sunset driving southeast with poor pavement
Extremely sunny with almost no clouds
Rows of trees directly next to road
Sandy side of road with occasional hogweed and fireweed

title: Belgorod
description:
Black car A type and tilted left long antenna fall coverage
Very hilly with dark black soil
Agricultural fields are abundant, especially with sunflowers

title: South-West Vologda
description:
C type short antenna summer coverage
Very sunny
Straight road angles
Unique clearings between the road and the tree lines.

title: Rostov Winter
description:
Red car/No car with antenna gen 4 winter
Very dark soil with some snow
Occasionally will have black car with antenna

title: Novosibirsk Snow
description:
White car A type long antenna fall coverage
Snow everywhere
Generally flat
Foliage consists nearly entirely of birch clusters and rows.
Not to be confused with the Altai Krai white car fall coverage which tends to be hilly and has no snow.

title: Smolensk M1
description:
A type short antenna summer coverage
Dark sandy soil next to road
Will often see fireweed
The only other places that have A type with fireweed are Karelia and Leningrad, however neither have divided roads in A type coverage.

title: Abaza Road
description:
Black car B type long antenna summer coverage
Very hilly with vegetation consisting of various birches, pines and larches
Driving north which helps distinguish from the Tanzybey road
South of Abaza, there is a smudge to the front right of the driving direction

title: Tanzybey Road
description:
Black car B type long antenna summer coverage
Will often see snow capped mountains 
Very similar landscape to the Abaza road in Khakassia, however this one drives south instead of north

title: South of Chita
description:
Black car long antenna summer coverage
Green rolling hills with general Mongolian-Manchurian Steppe landscape
Always driving south/east
South of Khada-Bulak, the weather becomes overcast 
South of Karanor will have rain coverage.

title: Kolpashevo Fog
description:
Gen 4 no car August coverage
In typical Tomsk fashion, there is pole spam
Soil typically is very gravelly
Not to be confused with Buryatia, Sakha or Magadan fog
Buryatia fog areas are mountainous and are barely forested
Sakha has white car and fog can be a pinker color 
Magadan also has white car, is extremely mountainous and has a different soil color

title: Leningrad
description:
Black car A type long antenna
May coverage (some summer)
Northern vibe with slightly red soil, pines and occasional hogweed
Mostly offroads; no major roads

title: Kostroma May
description:
B type short antenna May coverage
The only other places with B type May are Moscow, Vladimir and Sverdlovsk however road quality, soil quality, hilliness and vegetation are usually enough to differentiate
Strange front smudge on northern part of road
Bad road quality that has occasional faded outer lines and no center
Some other Kostroma May roads are unpaved

title: Chelyabinsk M-5
description:
No car with antenna August gen 4
Sometimes antenna will not be visible, but landscape and season should suffice
Looks nearly September
Ural mountains visible in open areas, else heavily forested
Relatively high amount of traffic

title: Bashkortostan May
description:
No car gen 4 May coverage
Signature Bashkortostan red soil
Rolling hills with intermittent random inselberg-esque rock formations

title: Cherkessk
description:
White car B type tilted right long antenna summer coverage
This is basically all you need to know; see this combo of car meta insta send Cherkessk in a real game
Hilly urban coverage
Rocky paths typical of the south

title: Road to Komsomolsk
description:
White car A type long antenna summer coverage
Presence of birches separates this road from Primorsky 
Mountainous with intermittent open fields

title: West Bryansk
description:
Black car blurred long antenna fall coverage
Relatively flat compared to other fall coverage western oblast regions such as Tula, Belgorod, and Lipetsk
Darkish soil accompanied by tall pines
If you find yourself on a flat and straight forest road in fall coverage, you’re probably in Bryansk

title: Tula Megalong
description:
Black car Megalong antenna fall coverage
Most of the landscape consists of rolling hills
Like many of the western oblast regions, has characteristically dark soil, but can be slightly lighter/sandier than that of Oryol or Belgorod
Unfortunately Belgorod, Bryansk and Tula can be hard to differentiate. Even with the antenna, it is no easy task. It usually is much more vibe based than anything that can be concretely detailed.

title: Don River Volgograd
description:
Black car blurred antenna fall coverage
Short and dead looking vegetation
Note lack of birch trees
Distinct rust brown soil

title: Tyumen Spill
description:
No car gen 4 summer coverage
Very sunny, with hardly any clouds in the sky if at all
“Omsk trees” 
“Tyumen grass”
Sometimes Omsk can be sunny as well so be sure to look at other context clues

title: North of Salekhard
description:
Red car gen 4 summer
Unlike the rest of Yamalo-Nenets, this area is decently hilly with the Ural Mountains visible in many panoramas.
Extremely short vegetation
Even urban areas are hilly, distinguishing them from other cities in Yamalo-Nenets

title: West Altai Krai Road
description:
B type short antenna
Back smudge with one side smudge
Sunrise south of Slavgorod
Very flat Siberian landscape 
Abundance of Russian olives
Railroad visible on many parts of the road

title: Perm
description:
No car with antenna gen 4 late summer coverage
Only other city with late summer and antenna is Chelyabinsk, which looks much more like September than August
Reddish-brown soil
Slightly hilly

title: Yaroslavl
description:
Black car B type tilted left antenna May coverage
As is the case with Kostroma, Yaroslavl tends to have terrible road quality
Slightly hilly with brown soil 
The landscape can be characterized as vast open fields with forest stands strewn about with relatively low vegetation
Western Ivanovo also has tilted left May coverage in addition to it having tilted left June. Use other context clues to differentiate between the two

title: Gorno-Altaysk
description:
B type short antenna summer coverage
Front smudge in the city proper
Very mountainous
South road will have Katun river visible to the west at some points
With back smudge and one side smudge, the only other place that will have mountains in B type is Kemerovo where they are not tall nor as close to the road as they are in Altai Republic

title: Kirov R-169
description:
Black car tilted right long antenna summer coverage
Driving north
Absolutely covered in hogweed in the northern parts of the road
Most of the road is lined with tree rows, whereas the south starts to open up
Southern bit of road is sunset

title: Smolensk Blurred
description:
Black car blurred antenna fall coverage
Very sunny with nearly no clouds in the sky
The west road drives north and the east road drives east
To differentiate between the two, the east road has contrails in the sky whereas the west road does not
Sunset coverage for both
Road quality varies from being unpaved to passable
As typical for Smolensk, very sandy sides of the road

title: Altai Krai Gen 4
description:
No car gen 4 summer coverage
Very flat with open agricultural fields
May look like Omsk, but the birches are in rows instead of clusters. In addition, there’s a wider assortment of foliage such as oaks and olive trees.
Very gravelly light brown soil

title: Mari-El
description:
Blurred short antenna summer coverage
Unique angle + driving north
Very sandy side of road
Both sides of road completely covered in pines
May have “Omsk trees” sometimes

title: Murmansk September SW Road
description:
No car gen 4 September coverage
Sandy side of road
Very rocky
Fireweed prevalent 
To differentiate this road from the SE Murmansk September road, this road has no red soil and most coverage on this road is post rain, thus the road appears wet, especially on the western part
